Item 1. Business

ACME Corp designs, manufactures, and sells rocket-powered roller skates and related anvil-delivery services to professional coyotes worldwide. The Company generates revenue primarily from hardware sales, with a growing subscription segment for cliff-edge warning services.

For a discussion of risks related to our single-customer concentration, see Item 1A of this Annual Report on Form 10-K.

Table of Contents

4

The Company operates in one reportable segment. International sales represented 12% of net revenue in fiscal 2025.

Item 1A. Risk Factors

Our business depends substantially on a single customer, and the loss of that customer would materially harm our results of operations.

Our products are frequently involved in high-velocity impacts with canyon floors, exposing the Company to significant product-liability claims.

12

Supply-chain disruption for premium anvil iron could increase our cost of revenue and compress gross margins.

Item 1B. Unresolved Staff Comments

None.

Item 7. Management’s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations

Net revenue increased 14% in fiscal 2025 to $4.2 billion, driven by higher unit volumes of rocket skates and a 40% increase in subscription revenue.

Gross margin declined 120 basis points to 38.1%, reflecting anvil iron cost inflation, partially offset by manufacturing efficiencies.

We ended the year with $1.1 billion in cash and $0.3 billion of total debt.

Item 7A. Quantitative and Qualitative Disclosures About Market Risk

We are exposed to commodity price risk on anvil iron. A hypothetical 10% increase in iron prices would reduce annual gross profit by $45 million.

Item 8. Financial Statements and Supplementary Data
